title: product-prd-unified-inference-pricing-packaging-roadmap-release-2027-08.json
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD requirements, high-level design notes, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments). The goal is to provide a single reference for product, engineering, go-to-market, and finance stakeholders for the 2027-2028 roadmap and the upcoming 2027-08 release.

1) Product overview

- Product name: Unified Inference
- TL;DR: A single API and operational surface that delivers predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with strong observability and rollout controls.
- Core capabilities: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming, function/tool calling, model routing and fallback, cost controls (batching, caching, quantization profiles).
- Primary users: software engineers, ML engineers, platform teams.

2) Goals and success metrics (2027-2028)

- Business goals:
  1. Increase Hosted API revenue by 30% YoY through improved unit economics and clearer packaging.
  2. Grow Dedicated seat bookings by 40% by promoting predictable latency SLAs and capacity commitments.
  3. Close at least 6 Private deployment deals with enterprise compliance requirements.

- Product success metrics (key results):
  - Avg cost per 1k tokens reduced 12% on common Gen-2 workloads by Q4 2027.
  - Median tail latency (P95) across hosted small prompt profile <= 120ms.
  - Adoption: 20% of active Hosted customers enable Redwood Optimize recommendations.
  - Churn: Active enterprise Dedicated customers retention >= 95% annually.

3) PRD and requirements (high-level)

- Functional requirements:
  - FR1: Unified API endpoints for text/generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking. Existing APIs must remain backward compatible for two minor releases.
  - FR2: Model routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region-preferred, canary. Policies configurable per-customer and per-route.
  - FR3: Redwood Optimize recommendations surfaced in Console: batching suggestions, quantization tiers, cache rules, expected cost delta.
  - FR4: Rollout controls: canary %, A/B traffic split, automatic fallback to compatible variant (e.g., quantized or smaller model).
  - FR5: Streaming responses with backpressure and resume semantics.

- Non-functional requirements / SLOs:
  - Availability: Hosted API 99.95% monthly. Dedicated: SLA as contracted (typically 99.9% to 99.95%).
  - Latency SLOs: P50 < 40ms for small prompts (<= 64 tokens), P95 < 120ms.
  - Cost visibility: per-request token-level cost and per-customer monthly cost breakdowns in Console.
  - Security: all Private deployments must support KMS/HSM integration and audit logging.
  - Compliance: SOC2 Type II evidence updated annually; Private deployments include required controls for GDPR data residency.

- Constraints and assumptions:
  - Backwards compatibility maintained for existing public SDKs for two minor releases.
  - Model catalog will include curated open models + vendor-provided variants; model performance profiles available for common sequence lengths.
  - Quantization profiles limited to validated hardware + model pairs; runtime must detect incompatible kernels and fall back gracefully.

4) Design / Architecture notes (high-level)

- Service components (owner tags):
  - API Gateway (eng-platform): authentication, rate limits, route policies.
  - Router & Policy Engine (eng-serving-runtime / eng-platform): selects model variant, region, and routing policy.
  - Serving Runtime (eng-serving-runtime): GPU-optimized inference engine (batching, KV cache, quantization-aware paths).
  - Optimize Service (applied-ml-and-evals): generates per-customer recommendations and quality regressions.
  - Console (eng-developer-experience): UI for recommendations, pricing preview, rollouts, and SLO dashboards.

- Key data flows:
  1. Request arrives at API Gateway -> auth & quotas -> Router consults policy -> route to Serving Runtime in chosen region/capacity tier.
  2. Serving Runtime applies batching & prefix caching; tokens emitted via streaming channel back to caller.
  3. Telemetry sent to observability pipeline (ingest -> trace enrichment -> cost attribution) for per-request cost breakdown and tracing.

- Compatibility table (example):

| Model class | Quantization tier | Hardware | Compatible kernels | Fallback variant |
|------------|-------------------|----------|-------------------|------------------|
| LLaMA-2 13B | int8 | A100 | optimized-attn-v2 | LLaMA-2 13B fp16 |
| OPT 30B | int4 | H100 | sparse-attn | OPT 30B int8 |

- Configuration example (YAML snippet):

api_route:
  name: customer-chat
  policy: latency_first
  model_variant: llama2-13b-int8
  fallback: llama2-13b-fp16
  max_tokens: 1024
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_wait_ms: 12

5) Roadmap & themes (quarterly, high-level)

- Q3 2027 (current):
  - GA Redwood Optimize integration for Hosted API (recommendations, cost preview).
  - Beta pricing tiers for Dedicated (standard / premium) and simplified Hosted pricing page.
  - Release: 2027-08 minor release (see Release Notes).

- Q4 2027:
  - Private deployment quickstart (VPC templates, kube ops package) and first Private customer pilot.
  - Expanded model catalog with 4 new verified model profiles for long-context workloads.
  - Improve routing engine for cross-region failover with <250ms failover detect.

- Q1 2028:
  - Advanced Optimize features: workload clustering, automatic batching policy experiments.
  - Packaging: introduce reserved capacity pooling for SMB/scale-up packages.

6) Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for GTM)

- Pricing principles:
  - Transparent unit economics: price per 1k input tokens and price per 1k output tokens where appropriate.
  - Separation of concerns: compute (per-token bill) vs reserved capacity (monthly commit) vs premium SLAs/retention.
  - Incentivize cost-efficient patterns: discounts for enabling caching or quantized runtime where quality is within customer tolerance.

- Packaging (recommended tiers):
  - Hosted Free / Developer:
    * Suitable for evaluation and low-volume dev.
    * Limits: 50k tokens/month, no SLA, access to baseline models.
  - Hosted Standard:
    * Pay-as-you-go per-token. Includes basic Optimize suggestions, standard models, 30-day logs retention.
    * Example: $0.60 per 1k input tokens, $1.20 per 1k output tokens for 13B-class models (indicative).
  - Hosted Pro / Business:
    * Volume discounts, longer retention, dedicated ingress throughput, custom rollout windows.
    * Example: 15% discount at $10k/mo spend.
  - Dedicated (Reserved Capacity):
    * Monthly committed GPU clusters with SLA-backed latency/availability.
    * Pricing based on vGPU-equivalent units, minimum 3-month commit.
    * Add-ons: 24/7 support, extended retention, private model onboarding.
  - Private (On-prem / VPC):
    * Platform license + annual support. Pricing varies by scale and compliance features (KMS/HSM, air-gapped packaging).

- Example cost analysis (sales talking points):
  - 100M tokens/month streaming generation, with Optimize recommendations applied (batching + int8 quantization) -> estimated compute cost reduced by 18% and estimated billed token cost reduced by ~12% vs baseline.

- Migration & discounts:
  - Offer migration credit for customers moving from self-hosted stacks (up to 3 months of discounted Dedicated pricing).
  - Early adopter Private pilot pricing with fixed engineering hours for onboarding.

7) Release notes: 2027-08 (minor release)

- Highlights:
  - GA: Redwood Optimize recommendations in Console for Hosted API (read-only with inline previews).
  - New pricing page and promotional packaging for Dedicated beta tiers.
  - Router: policy engine update to support percent-based canaries and automatic fallback to quantized variants.
  - Serving Runtime: int8 quantization path hardened for LLaMA-2 13B and OPT 30B on validated hardware; fallback logging improved for compatibility errors.
  - Console: per-request cost breakdown and P95 latency by route in the route dashboard.

- API changes / compatibility:
  - No breaking changes to public endpoints. New optional fields added to the /v1/generate endpoint: "routing_policy" and "fallback_policy". SDKs will be patched: clients should upgrade within two minor releases.

- Migration notes for customers:
  1. If you rely on deterministic fp16 outputs, validate quantized variant quality with your eval prompts before enabling Optimize auto-promote.
  2. For Dedicated customers, coordinate with Solutions to schedule a capacity cutover window; reserved capacity pricing requires a new contract amendment.

- Known issues:
  - INT4 variants are in experimental stage; not supported in GA.
  - Some long-context (>8k) models have P95 regressions under high concurrency; working on kernel improvements (eng-serving-runtime).

8) Rollout and launch plan

- Staging -> Canary -> GA cadence:
  - Week 0: Deploy to staging, run full perf regression suite (benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
  - Week 1: Internal canary: 5% traffic from internal beta customers + automated chaos tests.
  - Week 2: Customer canary: invite top-tier customers for early access.
  - Week 4: GA release and public pricing page update.

- Communications:
  - Product blog and release notes (public).
  - Email to existing Dedicated customers with migration path and discounts.
  - Sales enablement: one-pager, competitive positioning slide, example TCO calculators.
